question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot {8}^{5x-2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot {8}^{5y-2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot {8}^{5y-2} \\ \frac{1}{7}\cdot {8}^{5y-2} & =x \\ {8}^{5y-2} & =7x \\ {log}_{8}⁡({8}^{5y-2}) & ={log}_{8}⁡(7x) \\ 5y-2 & ={log}_{8}⁡(7x) \\ 5y & ={log}_{8}⁡(7x)+2 \\ y & =\frac{{log}_{8}⁡(7x)+2}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

    

Therefore, the inverse function is ${f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{{log}_{8}⁡(7x)+2}{5}.$
